# controlflow

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/controlflow"
```

Package controlflow determines whether execution can reach an if branch's value.

An if expression can contain statements before its final value. A return or jump can leave the branch without producing that value. For example:

```
name := if ready {
    if stopped { return }
    "ready"
} else {
    "waiting"
}
```

The first branch supplies "ready" only when stopped is false. The checker must check that value's type. Code generation must assign it to the result only on paths that reach it. Both compiler steps use this package so they agree on which paths need a value.

Branch reports two facts. Tail says that execution can reach the last statement. End says that execution can continue past the branch's end. These facts differ for a branch whose last statement is return: that statement can be reached, but execution cannot continue past it.

The analysis follows possible paths through loops, switches, and labeled jumps. It does not enter a separate function body. The caller supplies the rules that syntax alone cannot show, such as which calls terminate execution and which expressions contain TGo branch statements.

## type Result

Result reports whether a branch can reach its last statement or its end.

```go
type Result struct {
    Tail bool
    End  bool
}
```

### func Branch

```go
func Branch(body *ast.BlockStmt, syntax Syntax) Result
```

Branch follows all source paths through a branch. Jumps out of the branch end that path.

## type Syntax

Syntax identifies statements inside added expressions and Go control\-flow rules.

```go
type Syntax struct {
    RangeSourceOutside func(*ast.RangeStmt) bool
    Statements         func(*ast.CallExpr) ast.Stmt
    Terminates         func(*ast.CallExpr) bool
    Unevaluated        func(*ast.CallExpr) bool
}
```
